--accept-deprecated-v1-data.help: Accept deprecated V1 data field. (default true)

--additional-namespaces.help: Comma-separated list of additional namespaces to be scanned.

--all-namespaces.help: Scan all namespaces or only the current namespace (default=true). (default true)

--allow-empty-data.help: Allow empty data in the secret object

--cert.help: Certificate / public key file/URL to use for encryption. Overrides --controller-*

--fetch-cert.help: Write certificate to stdout. Useful for later use with --cert

--format.help: Output format for sealed secret. Either json or yaml

--from-file.help: (only with --raw) Secret items can be sourced from files. Pro-tip: you can use /dev/stdin to read pipe input. This flag tries to follow the same syntax as in kubectl

--key-cutoff-time.help: Create a new key if latest one is older than this cutoff time. RFC1123 format with numeric timezone expected.

--key-name.help: Name of Secret containing public/private key.

--key-order-priority.help: Ordering of keys based on NotBefore certificate attribute or secret creation timestamp. (default "CertNotBefore")

--key-renew-period.help: New key generation period (automatic rotation deactivated if 0) (default 720h0m0s)

--key-ttl.help: Duration that certificate is valid for. (default 87600h0m0s)

--kubeconfig.help: Path to a kube config. Only required if out-of-cluster

--label-selector.help: Label selector which can be used to filter sealed secrets.

--log-info-stdout.help: if true the controller will log info to stdout and error/warn to stderr. (default true)

--merge-into.help: Merge items from secret into an existing sealed secret file, updating the file in-place instead of writing to stdout.

--metrics-omit-secret-labels.help: When true, the sealed_secrets_controller_condition_info metric is not updated, so the metrics endpoint does not expose SealedSecret namespaces and names. Use this if :8081 is reachable by users who should not be able to enumerate SealedSecret inventory.

--my-cn.help: Common name to be used as issuer/subject DN in generated certificate.

--name.help: Name of the sealed secret (required with --raw and default (strict) scope)

--namespace.help: Default namespace to assume for Secret.

--old-gc-behavior.help: Revert to old GC behavior where the controller deletes secrets instead of delegating that to k8s itself.

--privatekey-annotations.help: Comma-separated list of additional annotations to be put on renewed sealing keys.

--privatekey-labels.help: Comma-separated list of additional labels to be put on renewed sealing keys.

--rate-limit.help: Number of allowed sustained requests per second for the verify and rotate endpoints (default 2)

--rate-limit-burst.help: Number of requests allowed to exceed the rate limit per second for the verify and rotate endpoints (default 2)

--raw.help: Encrypt a raw value passed via the --from-* flags instead of the whole secret object

--re-encrypt.help: Re-encrypt the given sealed secret to use the latest cluster key.

--recovery-private-key.help: Private key filename used by the --recovery-unseal command. Multiple files accepted either via comma separated list or by repetition of the flag. Either PEM encoded private keys or a backup of a json/yaml encoded k8s sealed-secret controller secret (and v1.List) are accepted.

--recovery-unseal.help: Decrypt a sealed secrets file obtained from stdin, using the private key passed with --recovery-private-key. Intended to be used in disaster recovery mode.

--skip-recreate.help: if true the controller will skip listening for managed secret changes to recreate them. This helps on limited permission environments.

--update-status.help: beta: if true, the controller will update the status sub-resource whenever it processes a sealed secret (default true)

--validate.help: Validate that the sealed secret can be decrypted

--watch-for-secrets.help: beta: If this is true, the controller will watch for key secrets. This is useful if you create the key secrets externally.
